subject: Taxes
title: Egypt's Tax Riots
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Egypt's Tax Riots.

hook.text: In 30 BCE, Egyptian villagers attacked Roman tax collectors with stones and clubs.

buildup.text: Rome taxed Egypt brutally: a poll tax per person, land taxes, and levies on trades. Egypt was Rome's grain supplier.

discovery.text: Tax revolts erupted repeatedly across Roman Egypt. Villages would collectively refuse to pay or flee into the desert.

twist.text: The Romans responded by holding entire communities liable. If one person fled, neighbors paid their share.

climax.text: Egypt's revolts failed militarily but revealed the limits of coercive taxation: force works until it doesn't.

punchline.text: Pay or flee. Egyptian tax revolts exposed the limits of force.

quiz.question: How did Romans punish tax-dodging in Egypt?
